rounds.response: I'm really sorry—having a manager point out a mistake can feel awful and it makes sense you're replaying it and feeling drained. Right now, take a 5–10 minute break (walk, breathing) to reset, then jot one concrete next step (correct the report or a quick note to your manager) to regain a sense of control. If you want, tell me the mistake and I can help you draft a short message or work through the thoughts; if these feelings keep happening, consider reaching out to a mental health professional for extra support.

rounds.response: You’re not being dramatic—feeling like one mistake means you’re “not good enough” is a common pattern (mindreading and overgeneralizing) and emotions often lag behind logical challenges. That doesn’t mean you’re failing; it means your brain is stuck in a familiar alarm mode and needs repeated, small corrective experiences. Try a tiny experiment right now: set a 5-minute timer to list 2–3 concrete recent things you did well, then send a one-line message to your manager clarifying the report or a brief check-in to your friend—small actions build evidence and reduce anxiety. If this keeps happening and interferes with life, consider working with a therapist for ongoing strategies; I can help you draft those short messages or walk you through a 5-minute grounding exercise now.
